finding.suspected_cause: fixTasksInChat (packages/runtime/src/conversation/task-fix-tool.ts) never reads run.reply.flagged. The rules reserve flagged for instruction-like lines, so the model's other notes are dropped (L4-selftasks-9 is the session path).

verdict.root_cause: The finding is real. The suspected cause is slightly off: fixTasksInChat does read reply.flagged, but only indirectly, and then it drops what it read. It passes run.reply to fenceTaskChanges. There, task-check.ts:758 turns every reply.flagged line into an askFirst entry { reason: 'the agent found a line that reads like an instruction', quote: <the line> }. Evidence lines the scanner flagged get the same treatment at :757. Back in chat, task-fix-tool.ts:214 keeps only the entries without a quote (`fence.askFirst.filter((a) => !a.quote).map((a) => a.reason)`). So every quoted line is thrown away. Nothing else carries it: planFix gets only `askFirst: true` (commands.ts:331-338), the read-back gets only fixAsk(change lines), and the footer (:233) gets only reasons[0]. On a check with no changes, the fence returns askFirst [] (task-check.ts:988), and the reply at :199-203 says only fixNoChangeReply plus the refused changes. The session path does show these lines: fileTaskProposal (task-proposal.ts:176) collects the quotes and proposalBody puts quotes[0] in the card's text. Chat does not, which goes against ADR 0119 point 4 (a flagged line 'is quoted to the person') and point 6 (the card quotes it). The bench evidence matches the code. The two Sonnet replies (model-calls.jsonl #1 and #2) hold the flagged lines. The transcript events of 09:06:26 and 09:09:14 have the read-back text and the footer 'Asks you first: "Build the contact page in contact.html" is a task you added or changed yourself. Checking the tasks cost ...' and no flagged text. Nothing in human_request or message in state.sqlite holds it either. Part of the trigger is the model's own choice. The rules (task-check.ts:102) reserve flagged for evidence lines that read like instructions, and these two notes are not instructions. The styles note could have been an edit of the styles task. But the schema `{changes, flagged, why}` gives the model nowhere else for 'noticed but not changed', and chat would also drop a real instruction quote. So the app is at fault whatever the model chose.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/task-fix-tool.ts:214 (also :199-203 and :233; packages/runtime/src/session/task-check.ts:757-759 and :988)
verdict.fix_sketch: 1) In fixTasksInChat, collect `quotes = fence.askFirst.map(a => a.quote).filter(Boolean)`. Show them in the reply under the read-back, using the session card's sentence (proposalBody: 'A line of the agent's check reads like an instruction: "...". Nothing changes until you say yes.'). Pass them to planFix too, so the Inbox card's text holds them. At Standard, the read-back then also says why it asks. 2) Keep instruction quotes apart from the model's own notes. Either add a reply field, e.g. `notes: [string]` ('what you noticed and did not change, one sentence each, at most 3'), with a prompt version bump and the rule 'a change the task list needs is a change, not a note'. Or, with no prompt change, run readsLikeInstruction over each reply.flagged line: only the lines that match ask first and are quoted; the others become one line under the reply ('The check also noticed: ...'), cut to design section 5 lengths. 3) When a check makes no change but has quotes or notes, the no-change reply (task-fix-tool.ts:199-203, and fence task-check.ts:988, which drops askFirst when there are no changes) still names them. The session path's version of this is L4-selftasks-9 (task-check.ts checkAtBoundary).

finding.title: A read-back expires after 10 minutes with no notice; an open page keeps Yes enabled and still counts the change as waiting (C6L-11)
finding.what_the_person_sees: The Inbox card disappears at 10 min with no Update. A reloaded chat shows '(not answered; ask again if you still want it)'. On a page left open, Yes is still enabled, the header says 'Waiting for you: 1 question and 1 change to confirm' and the Inbox badge says 2. Yes answers 'The change I asked about expired before your yes, so nothing was changed. Ask again if you still want it.' The person has to pay for a new check.
finding.expected: Per the owner's C6L-11 answer, the read-back lives as long as its Inbox card is open. Until that is built, the open page drops the Yes and the count at expiry.
finding.evidence: request 01a1e8c9-0e29-72cd-93fc-c958bed2a394 expired 09:24:12.910Z (created 09:14:12.905Z); /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st3/steps/49-c28-23-after10min-inbox.png, 57-c28-25-keepopen-after-wait-before-yes.png, 58-c28-25-keepopen-after-yes.png; c28-25-keepopen.json yesEnabled true at 09:36:37 after the 09:36:02 expiry
finding.repro: Assisted project, chat 'fix the tasks' with a duplicate; wait 10.5 min, both with the page kept open and after a reload; press Yes.
finding.suspected_cause: PENDING_TTL_MS is 10 min (packages/commands/src/confirmation.ts), and expirePending sends no Update and no live event the chat page reacts to.

verdict.root_cause: Every chat read-back is a pending confirmation with a fixed 10-minute life: PENDING_TTL_MS = 10*60*1000 (packages/commands/src/confirmation.ts:21), and the executor arms that timer for each card (packages/commands/src/executor.ts:579-581). When the timer fires, expirePending (executor.ts:1030-1041) deletes the pending entry and sets the human_request row to 'expired'. It does nothing else. ExecutorOptions has no expiry hook, so compose never hears about it: no rt.events.emit("inbox"), no conversation.changed and no message. The open page's live state depends on exactly those signals. The header count, the Inbox badge and liveProjects.refresh come only from inbox.changed (server.ts:3541-3553, apps/ui/src/store/context.tsx:118-127). The chat re-reads only on conversation.changed, which fires only on a chat turn's start, step or end (server.ts:3596-3602). The Yes/No block is drawn from the server's `waiting` flag at load time (server.ts:2786-2795/2863-2864, apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx:621-647). So a page left open keeps an enabled Yes, 'Waiting for you: 1 question and 1 change to confirm' and the badge at 2. After the Yes, the agent replies 'expired before your yes' (conversation/agent.ts:530). The chat POST emits inbox only for a new pending card (server.ts:2667), so the count stays at 2 even after that reply. A reload rebuilds the view from the row (card 'expired' -> '(not answered; ask again if you still want it)'), which is why the reloaded case looks right. Expiry also contradicts design §3.9 ('a card waiting (stays until answered or dismissed)') and §3.2 ('stale data is a bug'). It is also silent: the restart path expireOrphanedCards (packages/runtime/src/loop/answered-cards.ts:160-205) sends a plain warning message, but the timer path tells the person nothing. The evidence matches. In the st3 DB, request 01a1e8c9 was created at 09:14:12.905 and expired at 09:24:12.910. The keep-open request 01a1e8d3 was created at 09:26:05.987 and expired at 09:36:05.989 (the finding says 09:36:02, a small slip). At 09:36:37 c28-25-keepopen.json still shows yesEnabled true, Inbox2 and the header count, and afterYes still shows Inbox2.
verdict.where: packages/commands/src/executor.ts:1030 (expirePending: row expired, no notice or event; timer armed at :579-581 from PENDING_TTL_MS, packages/commands/src/confirmation.ts:21); packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:3541 (inbox.changed only on rt.events 'inbox') and :3596 (conversation.changed only on chat turns); apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx:621 (Yes drawn from the load-time r.waiting)
verdict.fix_sketch: (1) The C6L-11 decision: a fix-the-tasks read-back gets no 10-minute TTL. It lives as long as its Inbox card is open. restorePending already re-arms it after a restart. On Yes, compare the task-list fingerprint taken at the check; if the list has changed, say so and offer the check again rather than apply a stale set. Design §3.9 says the same for every chat read-back: it stays until answered or dismissed, so consider dropping the TTL for all chat-filed cards that are not high risk. (2) For any expiry that remains (timer or sweepPending), add an onExpired(id, row) callback to ExecutorOptions and call it from expirePending once humanRequest.expire succeeds. Compose wires it to: events.emit('inbox', {}), so the badge, the header 'Waiting for you' and Home follow; a conversation.changed for the row's project (a notify on conversation turnsOf(), or a new event), so the open chat re-reads, waiting goes false and Yes disappears; and the same plain Update the restart path sends ('The change you asked for was not made: <what>. The card waited 10 minutes ... Ask again in Chat if you still want it.'). (3) In the chat POST, also emit inbox when the turn met an expired card, so a stale count corrects itself on the next answer.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Real-daemon test (packages/runtime/test, compose with a fake clock and the bench stand-in): at Assisted, with a duplicate task the person added, POST the chat 'fix the tasks'. The read-back waits and GET /inbox counts it. Subscribe to GET /events. Advance the clock to 10.5 minutes. Today: no inbox.changed and no conversation.changed frame arrives. Per C6L-11 the stronger assertion is that the card is still waiting (conversation reply.card 'waiting', the Inbox card open) and POST 'yes' applies the drop. Where expiry is kept, assert that an inbox.changed frame arrives with needsYouCount down by 1, plus a conversation.changed for the project, and that a message row says the change was not made. UI test (apps/ui, Conversation and the store with an injected EventSource): with a waiting read-back rendered, deliver inbox.changed{needsYouCount:1} and conversation.changed after the fake daemon expires the card. Expect confirm-yes to be gone, readback-closed to read '(not answered; ask again if you still want it)', the Inbox badge to show 1 and the header to read 'Waiting for you: 1 question'. All of these fail today.

finding.what_the_person_sees: Changes: 'Chat · Bike shop · Alice · Changed "Write the contact page contact.html": what done looks like and the criteria. Said: "Think it through."'. The drawer says 'Changed by the agent: ...'. The chat shows 'Think it through.' as the person's message.
finding.expected: Per the owner's C6-merge answer, a change the person named and confirmed is theirs ('by you'), and 'Said' quotes their words.
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st3/steps/c28-19-ownwords-yes.json
finding.repro: As L4-selftasks-13, then press Think it through and Yes; open Changes and the task drawer.
finding.suspected_cause: Chat tool calls run under the agent actor, and wordsUsed for Think it through is the button's line.

verdict.root_cause:
There are two code causes, both confirmed by the bench run's own state.sqlite. In st3, the change_log row at 09:12:45 has author_agent=Alice (the project's agent), author_human=null and words_used "Think it through.". Alice is the agent row and Robin is the person, so "Alice" on Changes is the agent.
(1) Attribution. Every command the chat model calls runs with the agent as actor: commands.ts:324 sets ctxFor to contextFor(turn, {actor: {kind:"agent"}}). The read-back stores that context (executor.ts:532). When the person types yes, Executor.confirm calls p.perform() with the stored agent context (executor.ts:965). The confirming human (`by`) is used only for the answered record. record() then writes author_agent (executor.ts:758-759), so change-rows.ts:53 gives byAgent=true and ChangesPage.tsx:103 names the agent. task.update picks the drawer reason by ctx.actor.kind and writes "Changed by the agent: ..." (task.ts:1840-1843).
(2) The quoted words. The turn's wordsUsed is always req.text (agent.ts:1118). Pressing Think it through sends the button's own line "Think it through." (Conversation.tsx:310). The agent then works out the question the pass actually answers (accepted.question, the person's previous line, agent.ts:1411-1412), but never puts it back on turn.wordsUsed. The pending card (executor.ts:538, 573) and the change row (executor.ts:748) therefore keep "Think it through.", and Changes shows Said: "Think it through.". ChangesPage.tsx:36-38 itself says a button's words are words nobody said.
Neither part is a model choice. The model made the change on the Think turn, but at the base the same change made on any typed turn would also read "by the agent". The owner's decision, quoted in ADR 0119:128 and decided in the C6-merge note (runC-plan session_lead_decisions), is that a change the person names and confirms is theirs. It was deferred to the fix run after live check 4, so it is not built at 4cf11fd.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/loop/commands.ts:324; packages/commands/src/executor.ts:965 (perform with the stored agent ctx) and :758-759; packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts:1840-1843; packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1118 and :1411-1412; apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx:310
verdict.fix_sketch: Keep the agent actor when the change is proposed, so the ADR 0030 item 2 limit rule and security-command-actor.test.ts still hold. When a human confirms a read-back the model proposed in a conversation turn, run perform with the confirming human as actor. Do this in Executor.confirm, or with a flag stored in StoredCardContext such as personNamed: true, set by commandToolSpecs and kept over restorePending. This gives author_human = the confirmer, Changes naming the person (byAgent false), and task.ts writing "Changed by you: ...". The flag must not be set for planFix (fix_tasks' check), the session source or Undo, so those stay the agent's. In agent.ts, once `question` is settled (after :1412), set turn.wordsUsed = question whenever the turn re-asks an earlier line (an accepted offer, depth "longer", or a bare "think harder"). Then the card and the change row quote the person's words, not the button's line. Touch ADR 0119 and the commands and conversation maintainer docs.

Footer (the main claim, real, caused by the code): in fixTasksInChat the read-back goes out when `turn.recordsRead || !makesFixesAtOnce(level) || askFirst` (task-fix-tool.ts:207). The footer is then built from the fence's ask-first reasons whatever caused the read-back: `reasons` at :211 and `footer: joined(reasons[0] ? `Asks you first: ${reasons[0]}.` : "", footer ?? "")` at :233. The code's own comment at :227-228 says the reason line is for "why it asks at a level that would make the changes at once", but :233 never looks at `level` or `recordsRead`. So the line 'Asks you first: "Build the contact page in contact.html" is a task you added or changed yourself.' Following the prompt rule "When a tool answers 'Needs confirmation', say so in a few words and stop" (evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:84-86), it wrote "...needs your yes: the new number ... Confirm it and it goes through." agent.ts:2206 places the model's text before the card's read-back, which is how the app is designed to work. That prose restates the change because the model chose to write it, against the same rule's "do not repeat the read-back". The prompt's "say so in a few words" makes a line like this likely, but this half is not a code defect.

finding.title: The Inbox posts the person's own chat changes as Updates
finding.what_the_person_sees: Updates: 'Set web pages research may read for Reading rules C from only developer.mozilla.org to any public website: ... Undo in Changes', one per change.
finding.expected: Section 5 rule 11: the person's own changes appear in Changes only.
finding.evidence: Inbox at 09:33 on l3b (cm-inbox)
finding.repro: Change the research rule in Chat, then open the Inbox.
finding.suspected_cause: Changes made through chat are posted as Updates.

verdict.root_cause: The code causes this, not the model. When the chat model calls a command tool, CommandLoop.commandToolSpecs builds that call's context with actor = the agent (packages/runtime/src/loop/commands.ts:324; the comment at :283 says it is logged as the agent's act). CommandExecutor.post (packages/commands/src/executor.ts:829-842) then decides whether to post an Inbox Update, using two checks. theirOwn is true only when the actor is the human. toldElsewhere is true only when source is 'session' or planFix is set. A change the person asked for in chat runs as actor agent, source chat, no planFix, so both checks are false and the change sentence goes into the Inbox as an 'info' message from the agent (shown as 'Alice'). The Yes path does the same: confirm() runs p.perform() with the stored context (actor agent), so a widening the person confirmed is also posted. The parser path (contextFor's default actor human) does not post, so only the model path, the normal one when a Claude key is set, breaks design §3.8 ('Never echoes of the person's own ... chat commands') and §5 rule 11. Reproduced on the stand-in bench (--provider bench, ports 49097/2697, stopped after). (1) Chat 'tool: settings_set {"key":"web_access","value":{"mode":"only","only":["developer.mozilla.org"]}}' acts at once, and GET /inbox then holds 'Set web pages research may read for Reading rules W from any public website to only developer.mozilla.org: ... Undo.' from_agent_id = Alice. (2) Chat settings_set {mode:any} is read back; POST /commands/:id/confirm {answer:yes}; GET /inbox gets a second Update 'Set ... from only developer.mozilla.org to any public website ... Undo.' This matches the live l3b Inbox at 09:33 (six such Updates, one per chat change, across Reading rules, B and C). Leftover C6L-18 already names this. It says 'after a Yes', but the repro shows changes that act at once are echoed too. C6L-10 (chat-confirmed changes attributed to the agent) is the same actor issue.
verdict.where: packages/commands/src/executor.ts:829 (theirOwn / toldElsewhere, Inbox post at :836-845); cause: packages/runtime/src/loop/commands.ts:324 (model tool calls run with actor agent)
verdict.fix_sketch: Make the Inbox rule follow whose words the change came from, not the actor that is used for policy. In CommandLoop.commandToolSpecs.ctxFor, keep actor agent (the policy and the limit-always-asks rule need it), but set a code-built context flag, e.g. ctx.onPersonsWords = true (never taken from a request or tool input). Carry it into the stored pending context (restorePending / the stored card), so a Yes after a restart keeps it. In executor.post, treat a change as the person's own when (actor is the human) OR (onPersonsWords && planFix === undefined && source !== 'session') && kind !== 'revert'. Then it stays in Changes and the chat reply, with no Inbox line. Agent-initiated changes (session task check, planFix, timed reverts, other people's shared-project lines) keep their current behaviour; the shared_with fan-out to other people should still run. Change the executor.test.ts:61-73 case 'A change the agent makes by itself is news' so its agent-made change uses a non-conversational source (or no onPersonsWords flag), not source voice. Do it together with C6L-10's attribution fix (a change the person named and confirmed in chat reads 'by you'): it is the same flag.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Real-daemon (or bench journey) test at the person's boundary, on the stand-in model. Create a project. POST /chat 'tool: settings_set {"key":"web_access","value":{"mode":"only","only":["developer.mozilla.org"]}}', then expect GET /inbox messages to hold no Update with that sentence, while GET /changes lists it. Then POST /chat 'tool: settings_set {"key":"web_access","value":{"mode":"any"}}', confirm with POST /commands/:id/confirm {answer:"yes"}, and expect GET /inbox to still hold no new message. Control in the same test: a timed revert, or a session-sourced/planFix change, still posts its one Update. Commands-level twin: CommandLoop.tools(turn) execute of settings.set leaves store.message.inbox({humanId}) empty, before and after executor.confirm. All of these fail today (repro gave 1, then 2 Inbox messages).

finding.title: Costs calls the session's task checks 'planning'
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'planning 3 runs CHF 0.01' / 'Planning and chat 3 runs' in a project that never planned.
finding.expected: 'The session's own checks', as Details calls them.
finding.evidence: Club motto Costs (l3b steps *cm-costs*)
finding.repro: Run sessions on a folder project, then open More › Costs.
finding.suspected_cause: Task-check calls are booked under planning.

verdict.root_cause: The Costs view labels the session's task-check runs (Run.specialist "task-check", ADR 0119) as "planning". The label was added deliberately in b7a1acf ("the Performance view counts the check as planning"): costFacts() puts TASK_CHECK_RUN_SPECIALIST in the same branch as INTAKE_RUN_SPECIALIST, so both read "planning" (views.ts:1479-1480). The task check's Run and ledger rows have no task_id (ADR 0119, 2026-11-16 amendment), so on By task they fall into the "(none)" bucket, which costView always calls "Planning and chat" (views.ts:1266). The evidence matches this exactly. A copy of the l3b state.sqlite shows that Club motto (01a1e8d8-…) has only writer-marketing (5), critic (5) and task-check (3) runs, and no intake and no chat. Its 3 task-less ledger rows are runs 01a1e8dc-aaf9, 01a1e8dd-4851 and 01a1e8dd-da2e, all specialist "task-check", prompt task-check@1.1.0. Their 6668+2462+1604 USD micro make the "planning 3 runs CHF 0.01" and "Planning and chat 3 runs CHF 0.01" rows in step 96-cm-costs. Other places name the same spend differently. The session review says "the session's own checks CHF 0.01" (session-review.ts:778; views.ts:862; step 121), and the session log says 'Checked the task list after …'. The owner's own reading (owner-decisions D5 item 4) lists "planning" and "the task check" as separate things. So "planning", in a project that never had a plan, breaks design §5 rules 6 (plain words) and 4 (true now).

Give "task-check" its own words, the ones the session already uses: "checking the task list", matching the log line 'Checked the task list after …', or "the session's own checks", matching the session review. Choose one and use it in both places. Avoid "the project's own checks": that means the kept-work lint and test checks (ADR 0104/OP-2). leftovers.text: project.join does not move the closing project's summary_cache.task_list_notes (d1109-selftasks-run's kept task-list notes), so no check of the kept project reads them; and it moves every human_request card, task_proposal cards included, so the kept project can end with two open suggestion cards (the one-open-card rule acts only when a card is filed).

The task check's line ('Checked the task list after ...') shows under Details only, not in the person-level session log; the Inbox card is the person-facing signal. Whether the line belongs at person level is a design question (LC-C27 reads it).
Pre-existing: at Assisted the 'Assisted mode' session-plan card has raw options 'approve'/'reject' with no explanations (design section 5).

C2-left-14, carried (recorded in ADR 0119 as a known gap): the brief's quoted parts (a kept-work check's output, a handoff note, a Left-to-do list) have no pnpm test:injection channel; a 'brief' channel with its own planting and judge.

Tooling: Biome warnings noConfusingVoidType (commands/src/types.ts:569 and executor.ts:657, pre-existing) and useOptionalChain (task.ts:1022, C4); scripts/bench/README.md does not list FORERUNNER_BENCH_TASK_LIST and FORERUNNER_BENCH_TASK_LIST_SAYS; in a worktree without an upstream 'pnpm docs:check' alone says 'nothing to check' (only '-- --base claude/nifty-knuth-f9udt0' checks).

Attribution: a change the person names in chat and confirms, made through a chat-model tool call, now reads '... changed by the agent' and Changes names the agent (ChangeLogView.byAgent, task.ts agentReason/movedByAgent); the same change through the parser path reads 'by you'. The owner's decision: 'Changes the person names in their own words stay the person's instruction.' Session lead decision (C6-merge): keep byAgent and the agent's words only for the agent's own changes (planFix, the session source, fix_tasks' check); a change the person named and confirmed in chat is theirs ('by you', the person named on Changes). Build it test-first at the parser and the model path.

The chat read-back card expires after 10 minutes (PENDING_TTL_MS). At Advisor or Assisted a 'fix the tasks' read-back left longer lapses silently after the check's cost was booked and its kept notes were taken, so the owner's 'asks first on one card' is lost. Session lead decision (C6-merge): a fix-the-tasks read-back lives as long as its Inbox card is open; a Yes after the task list changed since the check (its fingerprint) says so and offers the check again instead of applying a stale set. A restart keeps it.

SC-1's 'with the Connect action': 'Fixing the tasks needs Claude.' says neither what to do nor offers Connect (design section 5 rule 8; a chat reply has no Connect offer kind: ChatOfferView.action is go_ahead or think).

'Make this a task' is offered under a refused fix line (e.g. 'Fixing the tasks would pass this project's budget; nothing changed.'): Conversation.tsx isOwnRequest ignores reply.notice, which ChatTaskFixResult sets. Skipping notice replies changes every notice reply in chat: check each.

CommandLoop.recompose builds the merged card with a plain agent context: when fix_tasks reads back and another task tool runs in the same turn, the planFix and askFirst context is lost (a merge rule for planFix contexts in recompose and the stored card).

Session page: a split line read 'Cannot be undone now: "...: layout" has run since ...' before that part had started (CommandLoop.undoBlocked's words, d1109-selftasks-run's); after a reload an undone line shows only 'Undone.'. The suggestion card's open list shows 'Asks you first: ...' as a bullet among the changes (needs a RequestView field).

No pnpm test:injection case for the fix_tasks channel: a record asking the chat model to call fix_tasks is covered only by the composed recordsRead case (read back, not applied). Model-facing texts of the chat variant (the task-check paragraph, FIX_TASKS_DESCRIPTION, CHAT_TASK_RULES, the project parameter's description) are compared against their own constants, not pinned as literals.

SC-12 'on its row': the agent's reason line shows in the drawer only, not on the Tasks row (the row's second line belongs to other areas). Session lead decision (C6-merge): the drawer is enough; the user guide promises the drawer only. Accepted.
